Prealgebra · Lesson 12.3

Draw a Picture

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Some problems arrive as a wall of words that is hard to hold in your head all at once. The strongest first move is often not a calculation. It is a sketch. A path becomes a map, a schedule becomes a timeline, and a set of clues becomes dots and arrows you can point at. Once the information is on paper, the answer is usually easy to read straight off it.

Problem
A baker slices a baguette into 99 pieces, and each cut takes 3030 seconds. Sketch the baguette with its cut marks. How many minutes does the slicing take?
Show a hint
  • Draw the loaf and mark the cuts. Nine pieces need one fewer cut than pieces.
Show the full solution

The sketch shows 88 cut marks producing 99 pieces, since each cut adds exactly one piece to the count.

8×30=240 seconds=4 minutes8×30=240 seconds=4​ minutes

Problem
A straight garden path is 180180 meters long, with a lamp at each end and lamps every 1515 meters in between. Draw dots for lamps. How many lamps line the path?
Show a hint
  • Count gaps first. The path holds 180÷15=12180÷15=12 gaps.
  • Dots outnumber the gaps between them by exactly one.
Show the full solution

The path divides into 180÷15=12180÷15=12 gaps, and the drawing shows one more lamp than gaps, since both ends hold a lamp.

12+1=1312+1=13​

Problem
Two boards, each 3030 cm long, are glued together with an 88 cm overlap to make one longer shelf. Draw the two boards overlapping. How many centimeters long is the shelf?
Show a hint
  • Laid end to end they would span 6060 cm, but the overlapped stretch was counted twice, once inside each board.
Show the full solution

End to end, the boards would cover 30+30=6030+30=60 cm, but the drawing shows the 88 cm overlap belonging to both boards at once, so it was counted twice.

60−8=5260−8=52​

Key idea
Count the gaps, not the things. Cuts, gaps, overlaps, and fences all have the same off-by-one trap, and a small drawing avoids it. Pieces outnumber cuts by one. Lamps outnumber the gaps between them by one. An overlap is length counted twice, so subtract it once. You do not have to memorize these, since drawing five dots shows which count is which.
Problem
On a straight boardwalk, the ice cream stand is 4040 meters east of the pier, and the arcade is 2525 meters west of the ice cream stand. Sketch the boardwalk as a line. How many meters is the arcade from the pier?
Show a hint
  • Mark the pier, step 4040 east to the ice cream stand, then step 2525 back west for the arcade.
Show the full solution

On the sketch, the arcade lands 40−25=1540−25=15 meters east of the pier.

1515​

Without the line, east and west blur together. With it, the subtraction is obvious.

Problem
A park drone takes off, flies 99 blocks east, 22 blocks north, 33 blocks west, and 66 blocks north, then lands. Sketch the flight, then find the straight-line distance in blocks from takeoff to landing.
Show a hint
  • Total the east-west motion and the north-south motion separately. The wandering collapses to one net east amount and one net north amount.
  • Net 66 east and net 88 north are the legs of a right triangle, and the straight-line distance is its hypotenuse.
Show the full solution

East-west nets to 9−3=69−3=6 blocks east, and north-south nets to 2+6=82+6=8 blocks north, so takeoff and landing sit at two corners of a right triangle with legs 66 and 88.

d2=62+82=100,d=10d2=62+82=100,d=10​

Opposite directions cancel, so a wandering trip always collapses to one net east-west amount and one net north-south amount.

Key idea
Draw the journey on a grid. Opposite directions cancel, so all the east and west steps combine into one net east-west distance, and all the north and south steps combine into one net north-south distance. Those two distances are the legs of a right triangle, and the straight-line distance from start to finish is its hypotenuse.
Problem
A claw crane lifts a prize 77 cm with each press of the button, but between presses the prize slips back 33 cm. The prize must rise 2525 cm to clear the bin wall, and once it clears, it is out, no more slipping. Draw the height after each press. How many presses does it take?
Show a hint
  • Track the peak height at each press. Press one peaks at 77, then each later press peaks 44 higher than the last, since 77 up and 33 back gain 44 per full cycle.
  • The story ends the moment a peak reaches 2525. Do not subtract the slip after the winning press.
Show the full solution

The peaks climb 7,11,15,19,23,277,11,15,19,23,27, gaining 44 per full cycle. The fifth peak of 2323 is still short of the wall, and the sixth peak of 2727 clears it, so it takes 66​ presses.

Dividing 2525 by the net gain of 44 misses that the winning press never gives back its 33 cm.

Key idea
How a gain-and-loss process ends. Some processes gain and give back on every step, like climbing and slipping, filling and leaking, or charging and draining. Draw one as a timeline, sketch the level after each step, and mark the first step that crosses the goal. The timeline stops there, and that last step counts in full, with nothing given back. Averages and net rates describe the middle of the process, not its end.
Problem
Four swimmers line up for a relay in positions 11 through 44. Kai swims immediately after Lena. Mira swims somewhere before Lena. Jo does not swim first, and Jo swims somewhere before Kai. Draw four slots and place the swimmers. Which position does Jo swim?
Show a hint
  • Kai immediately after Lena glues them into a block, Lena then Kai. Try the block in positions 22-33 and 33-44, since Mira must fit before Lena.
  • If Lena and Kai take 22 and 33, the only slot before Kai that is not first is taken by Lena. Push the block later and see what opens up.
Show the full solution

Kai right after Lena glues them into a block, Lena then Kai. If that block sits at 22 and 33, Mira takes 11 and Jo has no slot left that is before Kai and not first. So the block sits at 33 and 44, Mira takes 11, and Jo takes 22​. The order Mira, Jo, Lena, Kai fits every clue.

Four drawn slots turn each clue into a physical constraint you can test in seconds, instead of a sentence you have to keep rereading.

Problem
Five islands are served by ferries running both directions on these routes only. Coral to Palm, Palm to Bell, Bell to Coral, Bell to Drift, and Drift to Ebb. What is the smallest number of ferry rides that gets a traveler from Coral to Ebb?
Show a hint
  • Only Drift connects to Ebb, so any trip to Ebb must arrive through Drift.
  • Find the fastest way from Coral to Drift, then add the final ride.
Show the full solution

Ebb connects only to Drift, and Drift connects only to Bell, so the trip has to finish Bell, then Drift, then Ebb. Coral reaches Bell directly, so Coral to Bell to Drift to Ebb takes 33​ rides, and nothing shorter works.

Drawn as dots and lines, the dead-end branch out to Ebb is obvious in a way a written route list never is.

Fun fact
Drawing dots and lines for a connection puzzle has a birthday. In 17361736, the city of Konigsberg wondered whether a stroll could cross each of its seven bridges exactly once. Euler drew the land masses as dots and the bridges as lines, proved the stroll impossible, and accidentally founded graph theory, the mathematics behind every map app you have ever used.
Problem
A straight chord drawn across a circle splits it into 22 regions. Two chords can make as many as 44 regions, and three chords, drawn so every pair crosses inside the circle at a fresh point, make 77, as shown above. Keep drawing and counting. What is the greatest number of regions five chords can make?
Show a hint
  • List the maximum counts so far, 2,4,72,4,7, and look at the jumps between them. Each new chord adds one more region than the chord before it added.
  • The jumps run 2,3,4,52,3,4,5, so the fourth chord brings the count to 1111, and the fifth continues the pattern.
Show the full solution

The counts climb 2,4,72,4,7, with jumps of 22, then 33. A new chord that crosses kk old chords passes through k+1k+1 regions and splits each one, so the fourth chord adds 44 and the fifth adds 55.

2,  4,  7,  11,  162,4,7,11,16​

Drawing the small cases gave the numbers, and counting crossings explains why each jump is one bigger than the last.

Key idea
Draw the relationships, not just the numbers. Draw the finishing slots or the network, turn each clue into an arrow or a joined block, and place the most restrictive clue first. That is the tightest-condition rule from the organized-list lesson. A wrong placement contradicts a clue almost at once, and that one contradiction rules out a whole branch of possibilities. Sketches also produce small cases. Draw the one-chord picture, then two chords, then three, and use those counts in the pattern strategy.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A parade float rolls 1212 blocks west, 55 blocks north, and 1212 blocks east. Sketch the route. How many blocks is the float from where it started?
Show the solution

West 1212 and east 1212 cancel, leaving only the 55 blocks north.

55​

Practice
A kayaker paddles 99 km east, 44 km west, and 1212 km north. Find the straight-line distance in km back to the launch point.
Show the solution

The trip nets to 55 km east and 1212 km north, a right triangle with hypotenuse

52+122=169=1352+122​=169​=13​

Practice
In an elevator game, each round moves the marker up 66 floors and then back down 22. The marker starts at floor 00 and wins the moment it touches floor 2222, even mid-round. Draw the floor level round by round. In which round does the marker win?
Show the solution

The round peaks run 6,10,14,18,226,10,14,18,22. The fifth peak touches 2222 exactly, and the game ends there, no slide back.

55​

Practice
Four friends finish a race. Nia beats Owen. Pia finishes immediately behind Nia. Owen does not finish last. Quinn is also racing. Draw the four finishing slots. In which place does Owen finish?
Show the solution

With the Nia-Pia block at positions 11 and 22, Owen must finish after Nia but not last, which forces Owen into 33 and Quinn into 44. With the block at 22 and 33, Owen would have to take 44, which the clue forbids. So the order is Nia, Pia, Owen, Quinn.

33​

Practice
A jeweler cuts a long chain into 66 sections, and each cut takes 22 minutes. How many minutes does the job take?
Show the solution

Six sections come from 55 cuts, and 5×2=105×2=10​ minutes.

Practice
Twenty-five trees stand in a straight row with equal gaps of 66 meters between neighbors. How many meters is it from the first tree to the last?
Show the solution

Between 2525 trees sit 2424 gaps of 66 meters each,

24×6=14424×6=144​

Practice
Two boards, each 4545 cm long, are joined with an overlap to form a shelf 7878 cm long. Draw the boards. How many centimeters long is the overlap?
Show the solution

Without overlap the boards would span 9090 cm, and the shelf lost 90−78=1290−78=12 cm to the doubled section.

1212​

Practice
A subway map lists these two-way lines between six stations. A to B, B to C, C to D, D to E, B to E, and E to F. Draw the network. What is the least number of rides from A to F?
Show the solution

The drawing shows F hanging off station E alone. The quickest way to E from A is A to B, then the direct B to E line, and then E to F.

33​

The B to E shortcut is nearly invisible in the written list and impossible to miss in the picture.

Practice
Continuing the circle-and-chords pattern from the lesson, what is the greatest number of regions six chords can create?
Show the solution

The jumps climb 2,3,4,5,62,3,4,5,6, so six chords reach

16+6=2216+6=22​

Practice
A rectangular garden plot measures 5050 meters by 3030 meters. A gardener plants a flag at one corner and then every 1010 meters around the entire perimeter. How many flags get planted?
Show the solution

The perimeter is 2(50+30)=1602(50+30)=160 meters, which splits into 160÷10=16160÷10=16 gaps. The path is a loop, so the sixteenth gap ends exactly where the first flag already stands, and flags equal gaps at 1616​.

On a straight path flags would outnumber gaps by one, so line or loop is the whole question in fencepost problems.

Reading is a start. In the course you solve each problem yourself, with instant feedback, layered hints, and Milo right beside you when you get stuck.
